capabilities: Update created, updated, and viewed date properties automatically on edit or open
Count edits per note as an approximate activity signal
Bulk-populate missing dates from each file's on-disk timestamps with a dry-run preview
Reformat existing dates and rename date properties across the vault
Skip false updates using SHA-256 content hashing and gitignore-style file filters
extras: Requires Obsidian 1.13.0 or newer. Fully local: no network requests or telemetry. The plugin notes it has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff. Documentation on nested property limits, sync-cache exclusion, and date-format migration from Moment.js to date-fns is included.
intentEvidence: Obsidian has no built-in frontmatter date management. It tracks ctime/mtime at the filesystem level
motivation: The author lists the gaps it fills: manual timestamp upkeep breaks writing flow, sync services trigger false updates, template plugins write before templates finish, and old vaults lack consistent dates.
problem: Obsidian never writes date properties into notes itself, and sync tools or template plugins can create false or premature timestamps.

relations.evidence: making it queryable via Dataview for spaced repetition, review workflows
The plugin waits 5 seconds (configurable: Settings → Advanced → New file delay) before processing newly created files

summary: Automatically writes created, updated, and viewed dates into note frontmatter, with bulk fill, reformat, and property rename tools.
